Let $U={♣,♡,△,◻,♠,♢}$ be the universal set and let $Q={◻,♠,♢}.$ What is $\overset{―}{Q}?$
worked_solution:
The complement of $Q,$ denoted $\overset{―}{Q},$ consists of all the elements in $U$ that are not in $Q.$ To represent $\overset{―}{Q},$ we will shade in all the area of $U$ that is *outside* of $Q,$ as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14035973/assets/c94ed2827be8a72e798295f16870b4873940f5dffe5b8e17786985a97ccbacb0.png)

The elements in the shaded area are $♣,♡,$ and $△.$ These are the elements of $U$ that are not in $Q.$ Therefore, the complement of $Q$ is

$$
\overset{―}{Q}={♣,♡,△}.
$$
